2608.22802.title: SDoH-Aware Narrative Anchoring Bias in Medical LLMs for Trustworthy Clinical Decision Support
2608.22802.paper_summary: Medical large language models are often judged by how many clinical questions they answer correctly. That view is useful, but it misses a practical risk. A model may know the right answer and still change its response when the same case is written in a different patient voice. This paper evaluates that risk as SDoH aware narrative anchoring bias. We use NarrativeShield SDoH MedQA, a counterfactual medical question answering dataset in which each case appears in persona based narratives while the answer key remains fixed. The dataset is reshaped from wide format into case grouped persona rows. We evaluate three open source instruction tuned LLMs from the Qwen2.5 family: 1.5B, 3B, and 7B. The final experiment uses 300 clinical cases and produces 8,100 model responses across three prompting conditions. We report persona level accuracy, counterfactual consistency, correct consistency, and narrative sensitivity error. Qwen2.5 7B achieves the best accuracy at 56.33 percent and the best correct consistency at 40.33 percent. Paired McNemar exact tests show significant accuracy gains for 7B over 3B in all prompt settings. Even so, narrative sensitivity remains, with the lowest error still at 31.67 percent. These results suggest that trustworthy clinical decision support should be evaluated by both average correctness and stability across medically equivalent patient narratives.
2608.22802.paper_summary_zh: 醫療大型語言模型通常是根據它們正確回答的臨床問題數量來評判的。這種觀點是有用的，但忽略了一個實際風險。一個模型可能知道正確答案，但在同一案例以不同患者語音表達時仍然改變其回應。本文評估了這種風險，稱之為對社會決定因素(SDoH)的敘事錨定偏見。我們使用NarrativeShield SDoH MedQA，這是一個反事實醫療問題回答數據集，其中每個案例以角色為基礎的敘事出現，而答案鍵保持不變。該數據集從寬格式重塑為案例分組的角色行。我們評估了來自Qwen2.5系列的三個開源指令調整大型語言模型：1.5B、3B和7B。最終實驗使用300個臨床案例，並在三種提示條件下產生8,100個模型回應。我們報告了角色層級的準確性、反事實一致性、正確一致性和敘事敏感性錯誤。Qwen2.5 7B在準確性方面達到56.33%的最佳結果，在正確一致性方面達到40.33%的最佳結果。配對的McNemar精確檢驗顯示，在所有提示設置中，7B相對於3B的準確性有顯著增益。即便如此，敘事敏感性仍然存在，最低錯誤率仍為31.67%。這些結果表明，值得信賴的臨床決策支持應該通過平均正確性和在醫療等效患者敘事中的穩定性來進行評估。
